sections.h2: What does the Northampton County Register of Deeds do?
sections.html:
The office records, indexes and preserves the county's real estate records, plats, UCC filings and vital records. For a home seller, its main job is to record the deed that moves title to the buyer and any deed of trust the buyer's lender takes.

The county's own page says the land records reach back as far as 1741, marriage records start in 1863, and birth and death records begin in December 1913. Anything that has to be searched by hand is searched through paper indexes. Since the office also issues marriage licenses and certified copies of birth, death and marriage records, the phone line gets calls on many topics, so say you are calling about a deed.

The office page lists 252-534-2511 for questions. Ask there for the street address, hours and any closing schedule, since this guide does not print them.

sections.h2: How do I search Northampton County land records online?
sections.html:
Land records from January 1, 1991 to the present are free to search at northamptonrod.org. The county says this was the first time the records appeared on the internet, and the computerized index covers only that range.

  • Search from 1991 forward on the website for deeds, deeds of trust and releases.
  • For older records, plan on the hard-copy indexes at the office.
  • Use the parcel owner's name as it appears on the last recorded deed, since indexes follow the names on the document.

A chain of title for a family farm or an inherited lot often starts before 1991. If your parcel passed through several generations, call the office before you assume the online index shows everything.

sections.h2: Who is Northampton County and what does the housing market look like?
sections.html:
Northampton County is a rural county of 536.70 square miles of land with 16,491 residents on the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate. That is down 5.6 percent from the April 2020 estimates base and well below the 22,099 counted in 2010. Population density was 32.6 people per square mile in 2020.

The housing figures matter to anyone planning a sale. The Census Bureau counts 10,735 housing units, a 74.6 percent owner occupied rate and 7,857 households for 2020 to 2024. The median value of owner occupied homes is $114,500, median gross rent is $758, and 31.5 percent of residents are 65 or older. Only 15 building permits were issued in 2025, and 91.9 percent of people lived in the same house a year earlier.

Those numbers describe a county with older owners, long ownership and little new construction. Many sales here involve inherited or long-held houses, which makes a clean recorded chain of title more important than in a fast-moving market. The numbers come from Census QuickFacts.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Northampton County?
sections.html:
The fees are uniform across North Carolina, so Northampton charges what every county charges. An ordinary instrument such as a deed costs $26 for the first 15 pages and $4 for each added page. A deed of trust or mortgage costs $64 for the first 35 pages, then $4 per added page.

Recording fees printed by the North Carolina Association of Registers of Deeds (fee list updated February 5, 2024)
ItemFee
Instrument other than a deed of trust or mortgage$26 for 15 pages, $4 each added page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64 for 35 pages, $4 each added page
Plat$21 per sheet
Nonstandard document$25
Multiple instruments in one document$10 each
Satisfaction of a deed of trust or mortgageNo fee
Certified copy$5 first page, $2 each added page

The fee schedule is set by G.S. 161-10, which calls it complete and exclusive. The register collects it before filing, so the closing agent normally sends payment with the deed.

sections.h2: How does the transfer tax work when a house sells here?
sections.html:
North Carolina charges a deed excise tax of one dollar on each $500 of value or fraction of $500, and the seller pays it. G.S. 105-228.30 says the transferor pays the register of deeds before the instrument is recorded. Half of the money goes to the county general fund, and half goes to the Department of Revenue after the monthly remittance.

The county's page links a Deed Tax Certification form, a notice about deed of trust fee changes, and a redaction request form for public records. Ask the office whether your closing needs the certification form, because the register holds it with the deed.

sections.h2: What should I send to the office to record a deed?
sections.html:
Send the original signed and acknowledged deed with the payment and a self-addressed, stamped envelope. The county's page asks that every transaction include the envelope so the recorded document can come back to you.

  • Confirm the deed matches the standards the North Carolina Association of Registers of Deeds publishes on its recording standards page.
  • Include payment for the recording fee and the excise tax.
  • Mail it, or use the office's secure mailbox in front of the building, which the county page lists for drop-off.
  • Keep the confirmation of recording, because G.S. 47-18 makes a deed effective against lien creditors and later buyers only from the time of registration.

Priority follows the order of registration by time, so a deed sent late can lose out to a lien recorded first. Title companies usually record the same day as closing for that reason.

sections.h2: Which other county office matters before you sell?
sections.html:
The Northampton County Tax Department, at 126 E. Jefferson St. in Jackson, issues the bills that must be paid or paid off at closing. Its page says 2026 property tax bills are due September 1, 2026 and that interest will not begin until after January 5, 2027. You can call 252-534-4461 for the tax office, 252-534-5941 for land records or 252-534-3431 for listing.

The same page links appeal forms and a list of county property for sale. Ask the tax office for the current tax rate and a payoff figure before you set a closing date. If you want to skip repairs and showings on a Northampton County house, you can request a cash offer from Cash Home Buyers and compare it against your payoff and recording costs.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for Northampton County property?
faqs.a: Record it with the Northampton County Register of Deeds. G.S. 47-18 makes registration in the county where the land lies the point at which a deed takes effect against lien creditors and later buyers. Call 252-534-2511 for the office address and hours.

faqs.q: How much does recording a deed cost in Northampton County?
faqs.a: A deed costs $26 for the first 15 pages and $4 for each added page. A deed of trust costs $64 for the first 35 pages and $4 for each added page. The excise tax of $1 per $500 of value is paid separately by the seller.

faqs.q: Can I search Northampton County land records for free?
faqs.a: Yes, for 1991 to the present. The county says land records from January 1, 1991 forward are free at northamptonrod.org, and older records are searched through hard-copy indexes at the office.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed excise tax when a house sells?
faqs.a: The seller does. G.S. 105-228.30 says the transferor pays the tax to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded, at one dollar for each $500 of value or fraction of $500.

faqs.q: When are Northampton County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills are due September 1. The Tax Department page says interest on 2026 bills does not begin until after January 5, 2027, and North Carolina law adds 2 percent through the end of January and three-fourths of one percent a month after that.
